html:
Batu Khan was a grandson of Genghis Khan who led the Mongol conquest of the Rus lands and founded the Golden Horde.

He was the son of Jochi, Genghis's eldest son, who had been given the lands furthest west. In 1235 the great khan Ögedei sent Batu, with the veteran general Subutai, on a huge campaign to the west.

  • 1236: they crushed the Volga Bulgars.
  • 1237 to 1238: they burned Ryazan, Vladimir and other Rus cities in winter.
  • 1240: they took Kiev, ending Kievan Rus'.
  • 1241: Mongol armies beat the Poles and Germans at Legnica and the Hungarians at the battle of Mohi.

In 1242, after news of Ögedei's death, Batu pulled back to the lower Volga. There he built the capital Sarai and ruled the western steppe. Rus princes had to travel to his court to receive the right to rule, and pay tribute.

He opposed the next great khan, Güyük, and helped his cousin Möngke take the throne in 1251. He died around 1255. The Golden Horde he founded ruled over Russia for some two hundred years.
sum: Batu Khan was a grandson of Genghis Khan who led the Mongol conquest of the Rus lands and founded the Golden Horde.
